make.name: BYD
make.description: BYD Auto is the car-making arm of Shenzhen battery maker BYD Company (founded 1995), which entered the car business in 2003. It stopped building combustion-only cars in 2022 and now sells only battery-electric and plug-in hybrid vehicles, using its own LFP Blade batteries, and is the world's largest seller of plug-in cars. Its premium brands Denza, Yangwang and Fangchengbao are listed separately.

models.name: Dahan
models.description: BYD's flagship full-size sedan, sold in China from 2026 as an EV and a plug-in hybrid. Also called the Great Han in English; it was teased as the Han 9.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Launch version on the 1000 V Super e-Platform with a 102.3 kWh second-generation Blade pack and flash charging.

models.name: Han EV
models.description: Full-size Dynasty-series sedan launched in China in July 2020; the Han EV was BYD's first car with the Blade LFP battery. It was refreshed in 2022 and again for 2025, and a larger second generation was revealed in October 2026. A ride-hailing version was sold as the BYD e9 (now Linghui e9).

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Launch version on e-Platform 2.0 with Blade batteries; front-drive and 363 kW dual-motor versions.

generations.name: 2022 facelift
generations.description: April 2022 update with restyled bumpers, larger packs up to 85.44 kWh and a 380 kW AWD version; the 2025 model year (Sept 2024) cut prices and added lidar-based driver assistance.

generations.name: Second generation
generations.description: Larger e-Platform 3.0 sedan revealed in MIIT filings on 16 October 2026, slotting between the Han L and the Dahan.

models.name: Han L EV
models.description: Larger, higher-priced companion to the Han launched in China in April 2025; the EV version introduced BYD's 1000 kW Super e-Platform charging.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Launch version on the Super e-Platform with an 83.2 kWh Blade pack.

models.name: Qin L EV
models.description: Rear-drive mid-size electric sedan in the Dynasty series, launched in China in March 2025 and exported from September 2025 as the Seal 6 EV. Unrelated to the Qin L DM-i plug-in hybrid.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Launch version on e-Platform 3.0 Evo.

models.name: Qin Max EV
models.description: Stretched flagship of the Qin sedan family, launched in China in August 2026 as an EV and a plug-in hybrid with flash charging.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Launch version on the 800 V e-Platform 3.0 Evo with second-generation Blade packs; single rear motor of 120 or 240 kW.

models.name: Qin Plus EV
models.description: Electric version of the compact Qin Plus sedan, on sale in China since 2021 and facelifted in January 2025; the pre-facelift car is now sold to ride-hailing fleets as the Linghui e5. A second-generation Qin Plus EV appeared in MIIT filings in 2026.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Battery-electric twin of the Qin Plus DM-i with 47.5, 57 or 71.7 kWh packs; restyled in January 2025.

generations.name: Second generation
generations.description: Mid-size successor sharing the Qin L DM-i body; the EV version has been filed with a 100 kW motor.

models.name: Seal
models.description: Mid-size electric sport sedan in the Ocean series, launched in China in 2022 and exported to Europe, Australia and Asia from 2023. It was dropped in China in 2026, where the Seal 08 is now the Ocean flagship, but remains on sale abroad.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Launch version on e-Platform 3.0 with cell-to-body Blade packs of 61.4 or 82.5 kWh and an 800 V system.

generations.name: China 2025 model-year update
generations.description: August 2024 China-only update moving to e-Platform 3.0 Evo with roof lidar; the Seal was later dropped from the Chinese range.

models.name: Seal 06 EV
models.description: Ocean-series electric mid-size sedan launched in China in June 2025 as a sister to the Qin L EV; a lengthened 2027 model year version with flash charging followed in 2026. The Seal 06 DM-i plug-in hybrid is a separate car.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Launch version on e-Platform 3.0 Evo, rear drive, 46 or 57 kWh.

generations.name: 2027 model-year facelift
generations.description: Body lengthened by 150 mm to match the Qin Max, new 240 kW rear motor and second-generation Blade packs.

models.name: Seal 06 GT
models.description: Electric mid-size hatchback in the Seal family, previewed by the Ocean-M concept and launched in China in October 2024.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Launch version on e-Platform 3.0 Evo; rear drive or 310 kW dual-motor AWD.

models.name: Seal 07 EV
models.description: Battery-electric version of the full-size Seal 07 sedan, added in China in March 2026. An all-new, larger second generation was revealed in August 2026 and reached the market in November 2026.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: EV variant of the 2025-facelift Seal 07 body; single 240 kW rear motor.

generations.name: Second generation
generations.description: Larger 5.1 m sedan in Ocean Aesthetics 2.0 styling with second-generation Blade packs and flash charging.

models.name: Seal 08 EV
models.description: Full-size flagship sedan of the Ocean series, previewed by the 2025 Ocean-S concept and launched in China in July 2026 as an EV and plug-in hybrid.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Launch version on an 800 V platform with second-generation Blade packs and flash charging.

models.name: e3
models.description: Compact electric sedan of BYD's fleet-oriented e series, sold in China from 2019 to 2022; the sedan version of the e2.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Two pack sizes, 35.2 or 47.3 kWh.

models.name: e5
models.description: Compact electric sedan based on the petrol Surui, sold mainly to taxi and ride-hailing fleets in China from 2015 to 2020.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Electric conversion of the Surui; the e5 300 shared much with the Qin EV300.

models.name: Qin EV
models.description: Battery-electric versions of the original Qin compact sedan (EV300 from 2016, updated 2019) and of the 2018 Qin Pro; both were replaced by the Qin Plus EV.

generations.name: Qin EV (first generation)
generations.description: Electric version of the first Qin; the 2019 update carried a 53.1 kWh pack.

generations.name: Qin Pro EV
generations.description: Second-generation Qin sold as the Qin Pro; the EV had up to a 69.5 kWh pack.

models.name: Dolphin
models.description: Electric hatchback that launched BYD's Ocean series and e-Platform 3.0 in August 2021. Export models from 2023 are about 20 cm longer for crash rules; China got a facelift in 2025. Sold as the Dolphin Plus in parts of Latin America.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Launch version on e-Platform 3.0; 70 to 150 kW front motors and 30.7 to 60.5 kWh Blade packs. The 4290 mm global version arrived in 2023.

generations.name: 2025 facelift (China)
generations.description: March 2025 China update: new front and rear (length up 130 mm to 4280 mm), new dashboard and God's Eye C driver assistance as standard.

models.name: Seagull
models.description: BYD's cheapest electric car, a five-door city car launched in China in April 2023. Exported as the Dolphin Mini (Latin America), Dolphin Surf (Europe) and Atto 1 (Asia-Pacific, Australia). An all-new, larger rear-drive second generation went on sale in China on 20 October 2026.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Front-drive city car on e-Platform 3.0; export versions are longer and more powerful.

generations.name: Second generation
generations.description: Grown to 4205 mm with five seats, rear-wheel drive, multi-link rear suspension and flash charging on the larger pack.

models.name: e2
models.description: Compact electric hatchback of BYD's e series (sedan version: e3), sold in China from 2019 and facelifted in 2023 with a 43.2 kWh pack.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: 35.2 or 47.3 kWh packs at launch; the 2023 facelift moved to a single 43.2 kWh Blade pack and 95 hp motor.

models.name: e1
models.description: Small electric city car of BYD's e series, an electric revival of the F0 body sold in China in 2019 and 2020.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Single 45 kW front motor.

models.name: Racco
models.description: Electric kei car with a rear sliding door, built for Japan and launched there on 28 July 2026; BYD's first purpose-built kei car.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Two Blade pack sizes and a 47 kW front motor.

models.name: Atto 3
models.description: Compact electric SUV sold in China as the Yuan Plus from February 2022 and exported worldwide as the Atto 3, for many countries BYD's first car. It passed one million sales in June 2025. The 2026 Atto 3 Evo adds rear- and all-wheel drive, while China switched to an all-new rear-drive Yuan Plus in May 2026 (to be exported as the Atto 5).

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Launch version on e-Platform 3.0 with a 150 kW front motor and 49.92 or 60.48 kWh Blade packs.

generations.name: Facelift / Atto 3 Evo
generations.description: 2025 China facelift with new bumpers and DiPilot; exported from early 2026 as the Atto 3 Evo with a 74.8 kWh pack, rear or all-wheel drive and 220 kW DC charging.

generations.name: Second generation (Yuan Plus)
generations.description: All-new rear-drive Yuan Plus for China (May 2026) with second-generation Blade packs, 800 V and flash charging; export name Atto 5.

models.name: Atto 2
models.description: Subcompact electric SUV launched in China as the Yuan Up in March 2024 and exported as the Atto 2 (Europe, Australia), Yuan Pro (Latin America) and S1 Pro (Costa Rica). A plug-in hybrid Atto 2 DM-i followed in late 2025.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Front-drive on e-Platform 3.0; export versions use larger 51 or 64 kWh packs.

models.name: Yuan EV / Yuan Pro
models.description: BYD's first subcompact electric crossover: the Yuan EV (2016, export name S1 EV), the shorter S2 (2019) and the 2021 Yuan Pro facelift with a Blade pack. Replaced by the Yuan Up (Atto 2) in 2024.

generations.name: Yuan EV
generations.description: Electric Yuan; 2018 Dragon Face facelift added the EV360 (about 42-43 kWh) and EV535 (53.2 kWh).

generations.name: Yuan Pro
generations.description: 2021 facelift with Han-style front and a 50.1 kWh Blade battery.

models.name: Song EV / Song Pro EV
models.description: Electric versions of the first-generation Song compact crossover (EV300/EV400, from 2016) and of the 2019 Song Pro. Both have left the Chinese line-up.

generations.name: Song EV
generations.description: Song EV300 (48 kWh) and EV400 (62 kWh).

generations.name: Song Pro EV
generations.description: Electric Song Pro with a 71 kWh NMC pack and 135 kW.

models.name: Song Plus EV / Seal U EV
models.description: Electric version of the mid-size Song Plus crossover, on sale in China from April 2021 and exported as the Seal U EV in Europe from 2024. The Chinese model ended in 2025; export production continues.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Launch EV with a 71.7 kWh Blade pack and 135 kW front motor.

generations.name: Champion Edition facelift / Seal U
generations.description: June 2023 facelift with the BYD logo; exported as the Seal U EV (Europe) with 71.8 or 87 kWh.

models.name: Song L EV
models.description: Electric mid-size shooting-brake-style SUV in the Dynasty series, launched in China in December 2023; a rival to the Tesla Model Y.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: e-Platform 3.0 Evo; rear drive or 380 kW AWD.

models.name: Song Ultra EV
models.description: Mid-size Dynasty-series SUV unveiled on 5 March 2026 and launched in China at the end of that month, with second-generation Blade packs.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Rear-drive launch version.

models.name: Sealion 05 EV
models.description: Compact rear-drive electric SUV in the Ocean series, launched in China on 25 March 2025 and facelifted with flash charging for 2026. Not the same car as the overseas Sealion 5.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: e-Platform 3.0 Evo; 50 or 60.9 kWh Blade packs.

generations.name: 2026 facelift
generations.description: Mild restyle, longer body (4620 mm) and flash charging with second-generation Blade packs.

models.name: Sealion 06 EV
models.description: Mid-size Ocean-series SUV launched in China in July 2025 as an EV and DM-i plug-in hybrid; the EV was refreshed in March 2026 with up to 710 km and flash charging.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: e-Platform 3.0 Evo; rear drive at launch, dual-motor AWD option.

generations.name: 2026 refresh
generations.description: March 2026 update with second-generation Blade packs, flash charging and up to 710 km CLTC.

models.name: Sealion 7
models.description: Electric mid-size coupe-SUV launched in China as the Sea Lion 07 EV in May 2024 and exported as the Sealion 7 from late 2024 (Europe, Australia, India). BYD dropped it from the Chinese market in mid-2026 after more than 215,000 sales; export sales continue.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: China cars use 800 V e-Platform 3.0 Evo; most export cars use 400 V e-Platform 3.0 with different packs.

models.name: Sealion 08 EV
models.description: Full-size Ocean-series SUV unveiled at the April 2026 Beijing show alongside the Seal 08, offered as an EV and plug-in hybrid with flash charging.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: 800 V platform with second-generation Blade packs of 92 or 115 kWh.

models.name: Tang EV
models.description: Seven-seat Dynasty-series SUV. The second-generation Tang (2018) added battery-electric versions from 2019, exported to Europe from 2021 and sold in Brazil as the Tan EV; the Chinese EV ended in 2025. A third-generation Tang with EV versions was revealed in July 2026.

generations.name: Second generation (Tang EV)
generations.description: Tang EV600 and EV600D, later 86.4 kWh; Europe launch in Norway in 2021.

generations.name: 2022 facelift
generations.description: Grille-less EV front and a 108.8 kWh Blade battery.

generations.name: Third generation
generations.description: Revealed in MIIT filings on 10 July 2026; Datang-style design, second-generation Blade packs of 88.7 or 105.8 kWh and flash charging.

models.name: Tang L EV
models.description: Large Dynasty-series SUV launched in China in April 2025 on the 1000 kW Super e-Platform, positioned above the Tang. Plug-in hybrid versions are exported as the Sealion 8 / Atto 8.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Super e-Platform with a 100.5 kWh Blade pack and 1000 kW peak charging.

models.name: Datang EV
models.description: BYD's flagship full-size SUV (Great Tang), previewed by the 2025 Dynasty-D concept and launched in China in 2026 as an EV and plug-in hybrid.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Second-generation Blade packs up to 130 kWh and flash charging.

models.name: e6
models.description: Long-running electric MPV aimed at taxi and fleet use. The first generation (2009-2021) pioneered BYD's electric cars and ran as taxis in Shenzhen and abroad; the second generation (2021) is based on the Song Max and sold in China and right-hand-drive export markets.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Crossover-MPV with LFP packs of about 60 kWh at first and 80-82 kWh from 2016.

generations.name: Second generation
generations.description: Song Max-based MPV with a 71.7 kWh Blade battery and 70 kW motor.

models.name: M6 / eMax 7
models.description: Three-row electric MPV developed from the Song Max and e6, sold from 2024 in export markets as the M6 (Southeast Asia) and eMax 7 (India, Philippines).

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Standard Range 55.4 kWh / 120 kW and Extended Range 71.8 kWh / 150 kW.

models.name: D1
models.description: Compact electric MPV built for DiDi ride-hailing drivers in China, with a sliding rear door; sold only through the DiDi platform from 2020 to 2023.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Single 100 kW motor and an LFP pack.

legacy_notes.note: Han EV 'Flaship [sic] AWD', generation '2023': 510 hp / 516 lb-ft matches the 380 kW / 700 Nm 610 km AWD of the 2022 facelift, so claimed there. The Han is not sold in the US: the 320 mi 'EPA range' and model_webpage byd.com/us are wrong, and current_price 31400 has no currency or source.

Atto 3 'Design' is a UK/EU trim name of the 60.48 kWh Extended Range car; claimed on that variant. 'epa_range' 250 is not an EPA figure (not sold in the US; WLTP is 420 km). Price 39695 has no currency (looks like a UK GBP list price).
Atto 3 'Comfort' duplicates row 145 (same battery and motor; trim only). drive_type 'AWD' is wrong: the first-generation Atto 3 is front-drive only. Claimed on the Extended Range variant.

Dolphin 'Design' = export 60.48 kWh / 150 kW (201 hp) car; claimed on the Extended Range variant. 'epa_range' 250 is not EPA (WLTP 427 km); torque 229 lb-ft and top speed 99 mph copied from the Atto 3 row.
Dolphin 'Comfort' duplicates row 147 (trim only); claimed on the same Extended Range variant.

Seal 'Flaship [sic] AWD' = 390 kW dual-motor Performance/Excellence AWD, 82.56 kWh; claimed there. 'epa_range' 320 is not EPA (WLTP 520 km). The Seal was dropped in China in 2026 but is still sold in export markets.

gaps: Most Chinese (CNY) prices are missing: sources found give USD conversions or price ranges without per-trim mapping.
UK/EU/AU prices for export models (Atto 3, Dolphin, Seal, Sealion 7, Atto 2, Dolphin Surf/Atto 1, Seal U) not collected.
NEDC-only ranges (Han 2020, e-series, Qin/Yuan/Song EV, Tang EV, e6, M6) are not recorded because NEDC is not an allowed cycle.
Han EV 2020 Flagship AWD battery size conflicts between sources (76.9 vs 85.44 kWh); left null.
Qin Max EV and second-generation Seal 07 EV: motor/battery-to-range mapping not confirmed; some fields null.
Seal (China 2024 refresh), Dolphin (2025 China facelift), Sealion 05/06 EV (2026 refresh) have no variant rows: per-variant specs not sourced.
Racco range recorded as WLTC (Japan's cycle); the source calls it WLTP.
Linghui (BYD's 2026 ride-hailing brand: e5, e7, e9) and the BYD e9 Han-based taxi are not covered; not in this assignment's makes.
Images missing for several generations where no correct Commons photo of that exact version was found.
